component.name: Apache Ozone
component.description: Distributed, scalable object store (S3-compatible plus Hadoop-FS) built on Hadoop Distributed Data Store (HDDS), deployed as a cluster of network services. The Ozone Manager (OM) owns the namespace and metadata and issues delegation and block tokens; the Storage Container Manager (SCM) manages blocks and containers and acts as the cluster's internal Certificate Authority; Datanodes store data in containers, replicate via Ratis (Raft), and enforce block/container tokens when enabled; the S3 Gateway exposes an S3-compatible REST API to potentially internet-facing clients; Recon is a read-only management and monitoring service.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document (v1, ratified by the Ozone PMC); this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Ozone secure-mode cluster
blueprints.description: Cluster architecture described by the Ozone threat model in secure mode (ozone.security.enabled=true): untrusted S3 REST and Hadoop RPC clients reach the cluster through the S3 Gateway (AWS SigV4) and the OM/SCM control plane (SASL/Kerberos); Datanodes serve blocks gated by OM-issued block tokens when enabled and replicate via Ratis; SCM is the internal root CA for service identity; the CSI driver and test modules are out of scope.

assets.name: S3 Gateway
assets.description: S3-compatible REST API, potentially internet-facing; verifies AWS SigV4 signatures against per-user S3 secrets derived from the user's Kerberos identity. With security enabled, anonymous access is rejected.

assets.name: Ozone Manager (OM)
assets.description: Owns the namespace, metadata, and ACL checks; issues delegation and block tokens; reached over Hadoop RPC with SASL/Kerberos.

assets.name: Storage Container Manager (SCM)
assets.description: Manages blocks and containers and acts as the cluster's internal Certificate Authority, the root of service identity. Compromise of the SCM CA private key collapses all service identity by design.

assets.name: Datanode
assets.description: Stores data in containers, replicates via Ratis (Raft), verifies block/container token signatures before serving blocks when tokens are enabled; the token is the capability, the Datanode does not re-authenticate the user.

assets.name: Recon
assets.description: Read-only management and monitoring service for operators; in scope as part of the production cluster.

zones.name: External clients
zones.description: S3 REST clients and RPC clients outside the cluster trust boundary; untrusted until authenticated (SigV4, Kerberos, or delegation token). Authenticated users are trusted to authenticate but not trusted to stay within authorization.

zones.name: Cluster services
zones.description: OM, SCM, Datanodes, S3 Gateway, and Recon; inter-service identity is backed by SCM-issued certificates.

zones.name: Datanode Ratis peers
zones.description: Datanode-to-Datanode Raft replication peers; a peer holds a legitimate SCM-issued certificate but a compromised Datanode is a distinct Byzantine actor.

persona.description: S3 REST or RPC client outside the cluster trust boundary; tries to access data, bypass SigV4/Kerberos, or exploit the gateway. In scope.

Kerberos-authenticated principal acting within their granted ACLs; trusted to authenticate, not trusted to stay within authorization. An authenticated user attempting to read another tenant's data is in-model.
Trusted for the deployment: KDC, Ranger policies, SCM CA key, and network.

OM/SCM/Datanode services talking to each other and Datanode Ratis peers, authenticated via SCM-issued certificates. A compromised Datanode holding a legitimate certificate that behaves arbitrarily is in scope up to the Raft honest-majority threshold.

assumptions.description: A secure deployment assumes a functioning Kerberos KDC, time synchronization, DNS/rDNS, and a Ranger server if Ranger authorization is enabled.
SCM is the root CA; service certificates are issued and rotated by SCM and the CA key's secrecy is assumed.
Datanodes trust their local disks; on-disk encryption (TDE) keys come from an external KMS.
Admin, Ratis, and datanode service ports are assumed reachable only by the cluster and authorized clients (operator-enforced).
Secure mode (ozone.security.enabled=true) is the supported production posture; non-secure mode performs no authentication and is a development/sandbox posture only.

Several controls are off by default even in secure mode and must be explicitly enabled: object ACL checks (ozone.acl.enabled=false, Native ACL default authorizer when enabled, Ranger opt-in), block/container tokens (hdds.block.token.enabled=false, 1 day lifetime when enabled), gRPC TLS (hdds.grpc.tls.enabled=false), and TDE/KMS. Delegation tokens are enabled by default with security (renew every 1d, stop after 7d); token signing keys are SCM-issued HmacSHA256 symmetric keys with 9d expiry and 1d rotation.

threats.name: Unauthenticated request accepted on OM/SCM/Datanode RPC
threats.description: In secure mode, all OM/SCM/Datanode RPC requires Kerberos or a valid delegation token; an unauthenticated request being accepted violates this property. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Anonymous access accepted at the S3 Gateway in secure mode
threats.description: With security enabled, the S3 Gateway rejects anonymous access and there is no plan to support intended anonymous access (HDDS-7961); an unauthenticated S3 request being accepted in secure mode is a valid finding, not a disclaimed mode.

threats.name: Block or container access without a valid token in a token-enabled deployment
threats.description: When block/container tokens are enabled, a Datanode serves protected blocks and containers only on a valid, unexpired, correctly-signed token; block or container read/write without a valid token violates this capability gate. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Authenticated user accesses data outside their ACLs in an ACL-enabled deployment
threats.description: When object ACL or Ranger checks are enabled, volume/bucket/key operations are checked against the configured Native ACL or Ranger authorizer; an authenticated user accessing data outside their ACLs violates this property. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Rogue process impersonating a service on a certificate-backed path
threats.description: Inter-service identity is backed by SCM-issued certificates; a rogue process impersonating a service on a certificate-backed path violates service identity. Severity: critical.

threats.name: Consensus safety violation under the honest-majority bound
threats.description: Committed metadata or data must not diverge or be silently lost under the Raft honest-majority bound (standard Raft safety, for example 2 of 3 replicas for RATIS THREE; not Byzantine fault tolerant). A fork, divergent replica state, or acknowledged-write loss violates this property. Severity: critical, observable across nodes. Corollary: checksum verification on normal reads plus replica/container checks detect ordinary single-replica corruption.

threats.name: Plaintext on a transport configured for encryption, or unencrypted data when TDE is configured
threats.description: Hadoop RPC privacy, gRPC TLS, or HTTPS protect the wire when configured, and TDE protects data at rest for encrypted buckets when enabled with keys in a KMS. Plaintext on a transport configured for encryption, or unencrypted blocks when TDE is configured, violates confidentiality. Severity: high. An on-path network attacker is in scope where the deployment has enabled transport encryption for the relevant protocol.

threats.name: Byzantine Datanode forging data and metadata, or a Byzantine majority
threats.description: Ratis is not Byzantine fault tolerant: at or beyond a Byzantine majority of a Ratis ring, divergence is possible and out of scope. There is also no full guarantee against a single Byzantine Datanode that forges both data and metadata on the path it serves; checksum and replica/container checks catch ordinary corruption only.

threats.name: Leaked block token used as a bearer capability
threats.description: Block tokens are bearer capabilities: a leaked block token grants access until expiry (default lifetime 1 day when tokens are enabled). The caller and operator must protect tokens in transit with TLS; this protection is a downstream responsibility.

threats.name: Findings that only manifest in non-secure mode
threats.description: With ozone.security.enabled=false Ozone performs no authentication at all; this is a development/sandbox posture. Findings that only manifest in non-secure mode, or that assume ACLs, block/container tokens, transport encryption, or TDE are active in a default build where the operator has not enabled them, are out of model (non-default-build).

threats.name: Over-broad Ranger policy or world-readable ACL
threats.description: Ozone enforces ACLs and Ranger policies as configured; an over-broad Ranger policy or world-permissive ACL is an operator decision, not an Ozone flaw. Ozone does not author the authorization policy.

threats.name: Compromise of the KDC, Ranger, KMS, SCM CA key, or operator host
threats.description: The security-providing infrastructure Ozone depends on but does not own (Kerberos KDC, Ranger policy server, KMS and key material, network perimeter) and the SCM CA private key are out of scope; if the CA key is stolen, all service identity collapses by design. Side-channel and co-tenant adversaries against the host are likewise out of scope.

threats.name: SSRF, credential relay, and request smuggling at the deployment layer
threats.description: Well-known classes left to the operator or integrator: SSRF and credential relay via a misconfigured S3 Gateway, request smuggling at a load balancer in front of the gateway, and authorization-policy errors.

trustBoundaries.name: S3 Gateway trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Outermost boundary: untrusted, potentially internet-facing REST clients authenticated via AWS SigV4 over per-user S3 secrets derived from the user's Kerberos identity.

trustBoundaries.name: RPC/control-plane trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Clients to OM/SCM over Hadoop RPC with SASL; in secure mode authenticated via Kerberos or delegation tokens, with TLS/mTLS for gRPC where configured. Authenticated users are not trusted to stay within authorization.

trustBoundaries.name: Block-access trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: When block/container tokens are enabled, a client obtains a block token from OM and presents it to a Datanode, which verifies the token signature before serving the block; the token is the capability.

trustBoundaries.name: Ratis replication trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Datanode peers replicate via Raft; a peer holds a legitimate SCM-issued certificate but may behave arbitrarily if compromised. In scope up to the honest-majority threshold; Byzantine-majority divergence is out of scope.

controls.name: Run secure mode
controls.description: Set ozone.security.enabled=true for any non-sandbox cluster and require authentication on the S3 Gateway; non-secure mode is a development-only posture with no authentication.

controls.name: Kerberos/SASL authentication with delegation tokens on RPC
controls.description: In secure mode all OM/SCM/Datanode RPC requires Kerberos or a valid delegation token. Delegation tokens are enabled by default when security is enabled; OM delegation tokens renew every 1 day and stop renewing after 7 days.

controls.name: AWS SigV4 verification at the S3 Gateway
controls.description: The S3 Gateway verifies the AWS SigV4 signature of each REST request against the user's S3 secret (derived from the user's Kerberos identity / S3 secret store); with security enabled, anonymous access is rejected.

controls.name: Enable block/container tokens
controls.description: Enable hdds.block.token.enabled and hdds.container.token.enabled so that Datanodes verify a valid, unexpired, correctly-signed token before serving blocks/containers (BlockTokenVerifier, ContainerTokenVerifier). Off by default; token lifetime defaults to 1 day, signing keys are SCM-issued HmacSHA256 symmetric keys rotated daily with 9-day expiry.

controls.name: Enable object ACL or Ranger authorization
controls.description: Enable ozone.acl.enabled (off by default); Native ACL is the default authorizer, and the Ranger plugin can be configured instead via ozone.acl.authorizer.class. S3 multi-tenancy setup requires Ranger. The authorization property holds for whichever authorizer is configured.

controls.name: SCM-issued certificates for service identity
controls.description: OM, SCM, and Datanodes use SCM-issued certificates for inter-service identity (CertificateServer/CertificateClient); SCM is the internal CA and issues and rotates service certificates.

controls.name: Ratis (Raft) replication with honest-majority safety
controls.description: Datanode peers replicate via Raft, providing standard Raft safety under an honest majority (for example 2 of 3 replicas for RATIS THREE); Ratis is not Byzantine fault tolerant.

controls.name: Checksum verification on reads plus replica/container checks
controls.description: Checksum verification on normal reads plus replica and container checks detect ordinary single-replica corruption; this does not extend to a Byzantine Datanode that forges both data and metadata on the path it serves.

controls.name: Enable transport encryption
controls.description: Enable the relevant transport encryption (Hadoop RPC privacy, gRPC TLS via hdds.grpc.tls.enabled, and/or HTTPS) so block and delegation tokens and S3 secrets are not sniffable; rotate S3 secrets and review token lifetimes for the deployment. gRPC TLS is off by default.

controls.name: Transparent data encryption with an external KMS
controls.description: TDE is optional and protects data at rest only for encrypted buckets; it requires a configured KMS (for example via hadoop.security.key.provider.path). Isolate the KMS in a separate, firewalled network segment.

controls.name: Author least-privilege Ranger/ACL policies
controls.description: Author least-privilege Ranger and ACL policies; do not treat native ACLs as sufficient where Ranger fine-grained authorization is needed (or vice versa), and avoid world-permissive policies.

controls.name: Secure the operator-owned dependencies and network
controls.description: Harden and operate the KDC, protect the SCM CA private key, manage KMS keys, and network-isolate datanode/Ratis/admin ports. Non-secure exposure of these dependencies undermines the model.

controls.name: Protect service metadata stores at rest
controls.description: The OM, SCM, and Recon RocksDB stores hold critical credential and identity data; set restrictive file permissions and, ideally, encrypt them on disk.
